reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / WHO / India NTEP
clinicalPearls: The most severe form of tuberculosis, carrying high mortality and long-term neurological morbidity, and a medical emergency where treatment must not await confirmation
Onset is typically subacute over one to three weeks with fever, headache, vomiting, altered behaviour and progressive decline, in contrast to the abrupt onset of pyogenic meningitis
Cranial nerve palsies, particularly of the sixth nerve, and features of raised intracranial pressure are common, reflecting basal meningeal involvement
Cerebrospinal fluid classically shows lymphocytic pleocytosis, high protein and low glucose, though early cellular responses may be mixed
Basal meningeal enhancement, hydrocephalus, infarcts and tuberculomas on neuroimaging support the diagnosis
Cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification on cerebrospinal fluid aids rapid diagnosis and detects rifampicin resistance, but a negative result does not exclude the disease

Management combines prompt multidrug anti-tuberculosis therapy with adjunctive corticosteroids and neurosurgical intervention for hydrocephalus, guided under India's NTEP for extrapulmonary tuberculosis
reference.pathophysiology: Tuberculous meningitis usually develops when a subependymal or subpial focus (a Rich focus), seeded during earlier haematogenous dissemination, ruptures into the subarachnoid space. The released mycobacterial antigens provoke an intense inflammatory exudate that is most marked at the base of the brain. This basal exudate entraps cranial nerves, obstructs cerebrospinal fluid flow to cause hydrocephalus, and induces a vasculitis of perforating arteries leading to ischaemic infarction. The combination of inflammation, raised intracranial pressure and vascular compromise underlies the cranial neuropathies, strokes and depressed consciousness that characterise severe disease.
additionalInvestigations: Lumbar puncture with cerebrospinal fluid cell count, protein, glucose and opening pressure
Cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification and mycobacterial culture of cerebrospinal fluid
Contrast neuroimaging (CT or MRI) for basal enhancement, hydrocephalus, infarcts and tuberculomas
HIV testing and evaluation for tuberculosis elsewhere in the body
Repeat or large-volume cerebrospinal fluid sampling to improve diagnostic yield
redFlags: Declining consciousness, seizures or focal neurological deficit indicating advanced disease
Hydrocephalus or signs of raised intracranial pressure requiring urgent neurosurgical assessment
Rapid clinical deterioration mandating immediate empirical treatment before confirmation
Rifampicin resistance or HIV co-infection worsening prognosis
reference.prognosis: Outcome depends heavily on the neurological stage at which treatment begins; early treatment offers good recovery, whereas presentation with coma, deficits or advanced stage carries high mortality and frequent long-term sequelae such as cognitive impairment, hydrocephalus and paresis.
pitfalls: Withholding anti-tuberculosis therapy while awaiting confirmatory tests, allowing irreversible deterioration
Relying on a negative molecular test or culture to exclude the diagnosis
Missing hydrocephalus that needs neurosurgical drainage
Omitting adjunctive corticosteroids where indicated or overlooking HIV co-infection
management: Start antituberculous therapy urgently without awaiting confirmation, using a prolonged regimen with agents that penetrate the central nervous system
Add adjunctive corticosteroids such as dexamethasone to reduce mortality and neurological morbidity
Treat hydrocephalus with cerebrospinal fluid diversion such as an external ventricular drain or shunt, and manage raised intracranial pressure and seizures
Adjust therapy for drug resistance guided by rapid molecular testing and culture
Test for HIV and coordinate antiretroviral therapy, with attention to timing and immune reconstitution
Monitor for complications and long-term sequelae such as hydrocephalus, cognitive impairment and paresis, with rehabilitation input
